title: Introduce KMS constraint matrix and audit-enforcement hook with RBAC v2 condition evaluator
author: Priya Menon
description: Summary: Adds a KMS constraint matrix that declaratively maps tenant attributes and service roles to allowed KMS providers and regions, plus an RBAC v2 condition evaluator that checks kms:allowed_regions during token/operation authorization and an audit-enforcement hook that attaches signed audit envelopes to KMS requests. Motivation: customers operating with data residency requirements need stronger enforcement at the inference platform level so KMS requests are restricted by tenant policy and auditable end-to-end. This PR provides enforcement points at policy evaluation, request routing, and auditing to prevent accidental cross-region key usage. Design: 1) constraint matrix YAML (docs/compliance/kms-region-matrix.md) representing providers, region sets, and tenant attribute predicates; 2) condition evaluator integrated into rbac/v2 to surface kms:allowed_regions as a first-class condition that short-circuits incompatible key usage; 3) request-level hook in pkg/kms/enforcer that validates target key location, records decision to the audit log and attaches a signed audit envelope containing decision metadata and policy fingerprint; 4) migration CLI (cmd/admin/kms-migrate.go) that annotates existing keys with derived region assertions and generates a one-time report for ops; 5) integration+e2e tests exercising edge cases (multi-provider fallback, tenant attribute migration, and failure modes). Backwards compatibility: new evaluator is additive and disabled for clusters without the constraint matrix; feature flag redwood.security.kms_region_matrix controls enforcement rollout. Implementation notes: uses existing KMS abstraction so provider-specific checks are plumbed through provider adapters; signature uses current audit signing key and rotates via KMS signing wrapper. Checklist: ensure policy authoring docs updated; run migration in staging; verify audit retention export; coordinate with SRE for rollout and alerting. Testing: unit tests for evaluator and hook, integration tests using sandbox KMS providers, e2e scenario with tenant migration. Risks and mitigations: false positives on legacy keys mitigated by migration tool and flag; performance impact limited by caching region assertions and validating on key resolution path only. Related: ENG-2189 for policy editor work and SEC-412 for compliance review.

review_comments: Evan Carter: Can we make the migration idempotent? If the CLI is re-run we should not flip existing assertions. Author: Migration is idempotent, it only sets missing annotations and emits a report; updated CLI to no-op on existing tags.

Marta Liu: Audit envelope size could affect downstream KMS proxy buffers. Can we compress or use a fingerprint? Author: envelope contains minimal decision metadata and a policy fingerprint; added compression and unit test for envelope size.

Omar Hassan: Will this block cross-region failover in DR scenarios? We need a delegation escape hatch. Author: added operator-only bypass flag and an approval audit entry; escape hatch requires signed operator intent and is gated behind a feature flag.
Security review (Ana Ruiz): Ensure keys used for signing are restricted and rotated. Action: documented signing key lifecycle and added KMS signing wrapper integration tests.
QA (Ben): flake in e2e when sandbox provider returns 503; added retry with exponential backoff and improved test stability.
release_notes: Introduce KMS constraint matrix and RBAC v2 condition evaluator for kms:allowed_regions, an audit-enforcement hook that attaches signed audit envelopes to KMS operations, and a migration tool to annotate existing keys. Feature gated behind redwood.security.kms_region_matrix.
